Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about Redwood's routing and caching capabilities. We ran a small in-house sweep against our 1.5B LLM for the flows we mentioned and attached a stripped-down CSV of the latency/token counts (benchmark_results.csv) and a short model profile. 2) Pilot economics: we'd like to trial Redwood Optimize (batching + quantization advice + credits) over a 6-week pilot. Can you share what pilot credits or discounts you typically provide for a proof-of-value?

We're trying to finalize internal budget this week and would love a short written proposal so we can route approvals.

Hi Ellie — dug into the CSV and model profile. High-level, we see good opportunities for both batching and quantization:

Recommendations (short):
- Batching: use an adaptive batching window with a 12–30ms soft target and a max 80ms hard cap for your traffic shape. This reduces per-token GPU time while keeping p99 within ~10–15% of single-request latency.
- KV cache: prefix caching for FAQ-like prompts with TTL = 20–45s; set a larger shard for deterministic text generation to avoid cache churn.
- Quantization: we recommend trying int8 post-training static quant (PTQ) on the decoder blocks first; if you see >2% quality drift on your eval set, pivot to QAT-lite. For embeddings-heavy endpoints, keep higher-precision for the embedding head.

Estimated impact (back-of-envelope):
- Expected token-cost reduction: 25–40% with batching + cache on conversational flows.
- Model speedup from int8: ~1.6–1.9x depending on operator coverage and kernels.

Pilot structure we propose:
1) 6-week pilot (sandbox + production slice).
2) Redwood provides a 3k USD credit to cover infra for the pilot and a technical onboarding session.
3) One dedicated 2-week quantization pass from our applied-ML team to produce a recommended quant profile and an eval report.
4) Monthly overage pricing: 20% discount on hosted overages during pilot month if you commit to a follow-on evaluation window.

I attached a simple savings model (savings_model.xlsx) that maps your token counts to estimated consumption under three scenarios. Happy to walk through tomorrow — propose 30 minutes.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Product — Inference Economics | Redwood Inference

Ellie — appreciate the candid ask. Quick commercial response from Redwood: 

1) Pilot credits: we can do USD 4,000 in credits (applies to infra usage during the pilot only).
2) Concessions: instead of a blanket 30% off first-month production, we can offer 25% off hosted overages for up to 45 days post-pilot if PioneerOps commits to a 3-month evaluation term with a minimum committed spend of USD 12k/month thereafter (this is to protect engineering priority and capacity).
3) SOW: attaching a short SOW draft (SOW_draft.docx) and a pricing_summary.pdf for internal approvals; acceptance criteria in the SOW will be:
   - p99 latency under target (<=450ms) for the quoted traffic slice,
   - end-to-end token-cost reduction >= 20% vs baseline,
   - quantization report with MOS-like quality delta <= 2% on your evaluation prompts.

If that frame looks reasonable, we can route this to Legal and Finance and get a DocuSign SOW ready.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
